exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties

question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(4\mathbf{F} + \mathbf{G})$ at the point $(0,1,-1)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = ye^{x}\,\mathbf{i} + xz\,\mathbf{j} + (y-1) \, \textbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = z\, \mathbf{i} . \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(4\mathbf{F} + \mathbf G) &= \nabla\times(4\mathbf{F}) + \nabla \times \mathbf G\\[5pt] &= 4\nabla\times\mathbf{F} + \nabla\times\mathbf G. \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ ye^{x} & xz & y-1 \end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(y-1) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(xz)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(y-1)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(ye^{x})\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(xz) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(ye^{x})\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(1 - x\right) \, \mathbf{i} - \left(0 - 0\right) \, \mathbf{j} + \left(z - e^{x}\right) \, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = (1-x)\,\mathbf{i} + (z-e^{x}) \, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(4\mathbf{F} + \mathbf G) &= 4 (\nabla\times\mathbf{F}) + \nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = 4\left[(1-x)\,\mathbf{i} + (z-e^{x})\,\mathbf{k}\right] + z \, \mathbf{i} \\[5pt] & = 4(1-x)\,\mathbf{i} + 4\left(z - e^{x}\right) \, \mathbf{k} + z \, \mathbf{i}\\[5pt] & = \left[ 4(1-x) + z \right] \, \mathbf{i} + 4\left(z - e^{x}\right) \, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-1),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(4\mathbf{F} + \mathbf G))(0,1,-1) & = \left[ 4(1-0) + (-1) \right] \, \mathbf{i} + 4\left(-1 - e^{0}\right) \, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = [4 - 1] \, \mathbf{i} + 4(-1 - 1)\, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 3 \, \mathbf{i} - 8\,\mathbf{k}. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties

question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} + \mathbf{G})$ at the point $(0,-1,1)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \sin{x}\,\mathbf{i} + 3z\,\mathbf{j} - 2y \, \textbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = (6z-1) \, \mathbf{j}. \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

\begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ \sin{x} & 3z & -2y \end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(-2y) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(3z)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(-2y)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(\sin{x})\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(3z) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(\sin{x})\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(-2 - 3\right) \mathbf{i} - \left(0 - 0\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(0 - 0\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = -5\,\mathbf{i}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} + \mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} + \nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = -5 \, \mathbf{i} + (6z-1) \, \mathbf{j}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,-1,1),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} + \mathbf G))(0,-1,1) & = -5 \, \mathbf{i} + (6(1)-1) \, \mathbf{j}\\[5pt] & = -5 \, \mathbf{i} + 5 \, \mathbf{j}. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties

question.text:
Calculate $\nabla\times(\mathbf{F}+2\mathbf{G})$ at the point $(1,1,1)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where

\[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=x^2z\,\mathbf{i}+x^2y\,\mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z)=x^2z\,\mathbf{i}+(xy-2xyz)\,\mathbf{j}-xz\,\mathbf{k}. \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F}+2\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F}+\nabla\times(2\mathbf G)\\[5pt] &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F}+2\nabla\times\mathbf G \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

\begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ x^2 z & 0 & x^2y\end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(x^2y)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(0)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^2y)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(x^2z)\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(0)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(x^2z)\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(x^2 - 0\right) \mathbf{i} - \left(2xy-x^2\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(0-0\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] &=x^2 \,\mathbf{i} + (x^2 - 2xy)\,\mathbf{j}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get

\begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F}+2\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F}+2\nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] &=x^2 \,\mathbf{i}+(x^2 - 2xy)\,\mathbf{j}+2[x^2z\,\mathbf{i}+(xy-2xyz)\,\mathbf{j}-xz\,\mathbf{k}] \\[5pt] &=(x^2+2x^2z)\,\mathbf{i}+(x^2 - 2xy+2xy-4xyz)\,\mathbf{j}-2xz\,\mathbf{k}\\[5pt] &=x^2(1+2z)\,\mathbf{i}+(x^2-4xyz)\,\mathbf{j}-2xz\,\mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,1,1),$ we get

\[ (\nabla\times(\mathbf{F}+2\mathbf G))(1,1,1) = 3\,\mathbf i -3\,\mathbf j -2\,\mathbf k. \]

question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - \mathbf{G})$ at the point $(-2,0,3)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = ze^{y}\,\mathbf{i} + 3\,\mathbf{j} - x\,\mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = 2xe^{y} \, \mathbf{i} - 2e^{y}\,\mathbf{j}. \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - \mathbf G) & = \nabla\times\mathbf{F} - \nabla\times\mathbf G. \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

\begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ ze^{y} & 3 & -x \end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(-x) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(3)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(-x) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(ze^{y}) \right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(3) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(ze^{y})\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(0 - 0\right) \mathbf{i} - \left((-1)- e^{y}\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(0 - ze^{y}\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = (e^{y} + 1) \,\mathbf{j} - ze^{y}\, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - \mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} - \nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = (e^{y} + 1) \,\mathbf{j} - ze^{y}\, \mathbf{k} -\left[2xe^{y} \, \mathbf{i} - 2e^{y}\,\mathbf{j}\right] \\[5pt] & = (e^{y} + 1) \,\mathbf{j} - ze^{y}\, \mathbf{k} - 2xe^{y} \, \mathbf{i} + 2e^{y}\,\mathbf{j}\\[5pt] & = -2xe^{y} \, \mathbf{i} + (3e^{y} + 1) \,\mathbf{j} - ze^{y}\, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-2,0,3),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - \mathbf G))(-2,0,3) & = -2(-2)e^{0} \, \mathbf{i} + (3e^{0} + 1) \,\mathbf{j} - 3e^{0}\, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 4 \, \mathbf{i} + 4 \,\mathbf{j} - 3 \, \mathbf{k}. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties

question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf{G})$ at the point $(1,0,9)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = (2\sqrt{z}+ x)\,\mathbf{i} + xy\,\mathbf{j} + y^2\,\mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = 3x^2y \, \mathbf{k}. \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} + \nabla \times (-3\mathbf G)\\[5pt] &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} - 3\nabla\times\mathbf G. \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ 2\sqrt{z}+x & xy & y^2 \end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(y^2) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(xy)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(y^2)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(2\sqrt{z}+x)\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(xy) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(2\sqrt{z}+x)\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(2y - 0\right) \mathbf{i} - \left(0-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(y - 0\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y\, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} - 3\nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y\, \mathbf{k} -3 [3x^2y \, \mathbf{k}] \\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y\, \mathbf{k} - 9x^2y \, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y(1 - 9x^2)\,\mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,0,9),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf G))(1,0,9) & = 2(0)\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9}}\, \mathbf{j} + 0(1 - 9(1)^2)\,\mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3} \, \mathbf{j}. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle 3z, 2x, 0 \rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = xz+y.$ Given that \[ \nabla\times \mathbf F = \left\langle 0, 3, 2 \right\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \left\langle z, 1, x \right\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(1,0,0).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity: \[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get \begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ z & 1 & x \\ 3z & 2x & 0 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] & = \left[1(0) - x(2x) \right]\mathbf i - \left[z(0) - x(3z)\right]\mathbf j + \left[z(2x) - 1(3z)\right]\mathbf k \\[5pt] & = -2x^2 \, \mathbf i + 3xz \, \mathbf j + (2xz - 3z)\,\mathbf k \\[5pt] & = \left \langle -2x^2, 3xz, 2xz - 3z \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F} + \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] & = (xz + y)\left\langle 0, 3, 2 \right\rangle + \left \langle -2x^2, 3xz, 2xz - 3z \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0, 3(xz + y), 2(xz + y) \right\rangle + \left \langle -2x^2, 3xz, 2xz - 3z \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle -2x^2, 3(xz + y) + 3xz, 2(xz + y) + 2xz - 3z\right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \langle -2x^2, 6xz + 3y, 4xz + 2y - 3z\rangle. \end{align*}

Finally, \begin{align} \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(1,0,0) & = \langle -2(1)^2, 6(1)(0) + 3(0), 4(1)(0) + 2(0) - 3(0)\rangle\\[5pt] & = \langle -2, 0, 0\rangle. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle z, \sqrt{x}, 0\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = -z.$ Given that \[ \nabla\times \mathbf F = \left\langle 0, 1, \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \langle 0, 0, -1\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(4,1,4).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity: \[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

\begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ z & \sqrt{x} & 0 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &=[0(0) - (-1)(\sqrt{x}) ]\mathbf i - [0(0) - (-1)(z)]\mathbf j + [0(\sqrt{x}) - 0(z)]\mathbf k \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{x} \, \mathbf i - z \, \mathbf j + 0\,\mathbf k \\[5pt] & = \left \langle \sqrt{x}, -z, 0 \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F} + \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] & = (-z)\left\langle 0, 1 , \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right\rangle + \left \langle \sqrt{x}, -z, 0 \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 0, -z , -\dfrac{z}{2\sqrt{x}}\right\rangle + \left \langle \sqrt{x}, -z, 0 \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left \langle \sqrt{x}, -2z, -\dfrac{z}{2\sqrt{x}} \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Finally, \begin{align} \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(4,1,4) & = \left \langle \sqrt{4}, -2(4), -\dfrac{4}{2\sqrt{4}} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 2, -8, -1 \right\rangle. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle xe^{y}, z, 0\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = x - e^{y}.$ Given that \[ \nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle -1, 0, -xe^{y}\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \langle 1, -e^{y}, 0\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(2,0,-3).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity: \[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get \begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & -e^{y} & 0 \\ xe^{y} & z & 0 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] & = [-e^{y}(0) - 0(z) ]\mathbf i - [1(0) - 0(xe^{y})]\mathbf j + [1(z) - (-e^{y})(xe^{y})]\mathbf k \\[5pt] & = 0 \, \mathbf i - 0 \,\mathbf j + (z + xe^{2y}) \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] & = \left \langle 0, 0, z + xe^{2y} \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F} + \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] & = (x - e^{y})\langle -1, 0, -xe^{y} \rangle + \left \langle 0, 0, z+xe^{2y} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle e^{y} - x, 0, xe^{2y} - x^2e^{y} \right\rangle + \left \langle 0, 0, z+xe^{2y} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle e^{y} - x, 0, 2xe^{2y} + z - x^2e^{y} \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Finally, \begin{align} \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(2,0,-3) & = \left\langle e^{0} - 2, 0, 2(2)e^{2(0)} + (-3) - (2)^2e^{0} \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \langle -1, 0, -3 \rangle. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

question.text: Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle -1, 0, xy^3\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = yz.$ Given that \[ \nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle 3xy^2, -y^3, 0\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \langle 0, z, y\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(0,-1,2).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity: \[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get \begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 0 & z & y \\ -1 & 0 & xy^3 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &=[z(xy^3) - y(0) ]\mathbf i - [0(xy^3) - y(-1)]\mathbf j + [0(0) - z(-1)]\mathbf k \\[5pt] & = xzy^3 \, \mathbf i - y\,\mathbf j + z \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] & = \left \langle xzy^3, -y, z \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F} + \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] & = yz\langle 3xy^2, -y^3 , 0 \rangle + \left \langle xzy^3, -y, z \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 3xzy^3, -zy^4, 0 \right\rangle + \left \langle xzy^3, -y, z \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \left\langle 4xzy^3, -zy^4 - y , z \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Finally, \begin{align} \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(0,-1,2) & = \left\langle 4(0)(2)(-1)^3, -2(-1)^4 - (-1) , 2 \right\rangle\\[5pt] & = \langle 0, -1, 2 \rangle. \end{align}

question.text:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle xe^{y}, yz, 0\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) =xe^{-y}.$ Given that

\[ \nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle -y,0,-xe^{y}\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \langle e^{-y}, -xe^{-y}, 0\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(0,1,2).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity:

\[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

\begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ e^{-y} & -xe^{-y} & 0 \\ xe^{y} & yz & 0 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &=[(-xe^{-y})(0) -(yz)(0) ]\mathbf i - [(e^{-y})(0) -(xe^{y})(0) ]\mathbf j + [(e^{-y})(yz) -(xe^{y})(-xe^{-y}) ]\mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 0\,\mathbf i +0\mathbf j + \left(yze^{-y} +x^2\right)\mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 0, 0, yze^{-y} + x^2 \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] &= (xe^{-y})\langle -y,0,-xe^{y}\rangle + \left\langle 0, 0, yze^{-y} + x^2 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle -xye^{-y},0, - x^2\right\rangle + \left\langle 0, 0, yze^{-y} + x^2 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &=\left\langle -xye^{-y}, 0 , yze^{-y} \right\rangle \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(0,1,2) = \left\langle 0,0,\dfrac 2 e\right\rangle. \]
